Where the write-up was silent, B guessed the engineer's intent each time and resisted the concrete picture. It flagged four real losses: the post-overtop quantity ('Marks are checked against the quantities after overtop'), the bleed snapshot and state, washout rounding ('the remainder ceil(q/2) goes to waste') and form 6 into the tally. It resolved five others silently in its own rules: overtop capping to capacity, the 5-cycle run, once-per-cycle changes, simultaneous moves ('make every move at once') and the conservation formula. It also accepted the incomplete form-2-only note ('Form 2 ends at 10 ... The write-up allows this') without noticing that form 4 also ends over capacity. It treated the embedded Report figures as 'claims to check', but only in its notes, not as a flagged gap.

C also guessed the engineer's intent throughout. It flagged eight real losses: washout rounding, the waste-tally composition, the bleed snapshot and state, simultaneity ('mix that arrives by bleed does not bleed again in the same cycle'), the post-overtop check and once-per-cycle changes ('checked once per form per cycle on the post-overtop quantities'), the embedded answer ('Pre-filled Report figures'), and the incomplete over-capacity note ('form 4 also ends over capacity (7 against 6)'). It resolved three silently: overtop capping to capacity, the 5-cycle run and the conservation formula.

domainPull: The concrete language pulled hardest in the Bleed step. There the write-up says a HOT form 'bleeds half ... back up the chute into the form before it', which sends mix uphill, and lets HOT forms return to GREEN, which runs against irreversible setting. The pull continued in 'Nothing trims after this, so a form can carry over capacity', which contradicts what a physical form can hold, and in 'halve every form, rounded down', which leaves open which half is rounded. Nobody fell for any of it: B and C both applied upstream transfer, reversible states and uncapped post-bleed levels exactly as written. C's pre-read named the trap directly: 'Real concrete does not flow back uphill, and curing does not reverse'.
preReadNamedTheBreak: n/a: nobody fell. B's report is exact and A returned no report, so there was no failure for the pre-read to anticipate. C's notes did name the uphill-bleed and reversible-state traps and the embedded Report figures in advance.
preReadEffect: The pre-read helped with gap flagging and made no difference to the final numbers, which both B and C got exactly right. C flagged 8 real losses to B's 4, including simultaneity and the embedded pre-filled answer. It also caught the misleading 'form 2 over capacity' note, adding 'form 4 also ends over capacity (7 against 6)', which B missed. Its explicit commitment to 'Ignore real-concrete intuition' made its resolution of the domain traps deliberate rather than incidental.
summary: The write-up compresses or blurs about a dozen rules: the bleed snapshot and simultaneity, washout rounding, the waste-tally definition and the balance formula. It also embeds the full expected answer, plus an incomplete note that names only form 2 as ending over capacity when form 4 does too. B and C both matched the true answer exactly by following the engineer's rules over the concrete picture; A returned no report, so its failure cannot be traced to the document. C's pre-read did not change the numbers, but it roughly doubled correct gap flagging (8 against 4) and caught the form-4 omission that B accepted.
